A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QSpec research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material. Changed experimental settings limit direct performance comparisons but do not prevent assessing the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantization-quality evaluations, token-similarity measurements, throughput and latency results, and draft-length experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds measured EAGLE comparisons and acceptance-rate results across quantization methods.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 retains weight-shared W4A4 drafting, parallel W4A16 verification, greedy token acceptance, and KV-cache overwriting. The new tree-decoding analysis and discussion of compatibility with KV compression do not introduce a changed QSpec procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate WikiText-2, PIQA, WinoGrande, GSM8K, MATH, MBPP, HumanEval, ShareGPT, and LMsys-1K. Results omitted from v2's shortened main throughput table remain in Appendix A; the added comparisons do not introduce new datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 adds an evaluated EAGLE comparator using an FP16 draft model and W4A16 EAGLE-Quant target (Tables 5 and 8); v1 only discussed EAGLE as related work. It also adds W16A16 rows to the full fidelity comparison and W16A16/W4A4 baselines to throughput and latency comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported platform changes from four A100 40GB GPUs to four L20 48GB GPUs. v2 introduces an EAGLE comparison on Llama-2-7b-chat-hf at batch sizes 1, 8, and 16, with specified draft/target precisions, and reports pipeline parallelism for full-precision configurations that exceed memory. The draft-length range changes from 2–7 to 2–6, and Table 3 reverses the stated relative-degradation formula.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused Atom-versus-QuaRot acceptance-rate ablation on three datasets (Table 6) and qualitatively reports degraded acceptance when quantizing EAGLE's draft model. It narrows the documented draft-length analysis and revises the latency-decomposition configurations. These are limited extensions and revisions of the existing performance analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions retain dataset-sampling seed 42 and point-estimate reporting. Neither reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or statistical error bars. The additional results do not change uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Throughput and latency results are extensively replaced under the revised hardware, with the reported peak speedup changing from 1.80× to 1.64×. New EAGLE results include 260.48 versus 167.57 tokens/s for QSpec and EAGLE on LMsys-1K at batch size 8 (Table 8). Fidelity values also change: Atom-QSpec MBPP rises from 39.0 to 40.5 in Table 3, and W16A16 WikiText-2 perplexity changes from 8.70 to 7.73 in Table 1. These are reported result revisions, not established same-setting gains.

T1.justification: v2 Section 3.2 introduces a mathematical model of tree-structured drafting, an expression for expected accepted tokens H(k), and a per-valid-token cost expression involving C(k)/H(k) (Equations 2–3). v1 contains only the autoregressive sampling equation and qualitative advantage analysis.

C1.justification: v2 adds superiority over state-of-the-art speculative decoding in quantized batched serving as a headline contribution, claiming theoretical and empirical support and up to 1.55× acceleration over EAGLE. It revises the headline W4A16 speedup from 1.80× to 1.64× while retaining the quality-preservation, memory-sharing, and training-free claims.

C2.justification: v2 develops explanations linking batched-serving efficiency to tree-verification overhead and attributes EAGLE's memory failures to its draft KV cache. It newly discusses compatibility with KV compression. Conversely, v1 Appendix C's warnings about excessively large batches and failed termination tokens disappear; its small-batch and GQA explanations partly survive elsewhere.

D1.justification: v2 updates hardware specifications and documents EAGLE precision choices, batching restrictions, full-precision pipeline parallelism, and quantizer-specific sampling details. The fake-quantization/trace-replay procedure, CUDA version, group size, and default draft length remain. v1's disclosure of model-structure adjustments for Atom kernel shapes is removed, without establishing that those adjustments stopped.

R1.justification: Research positioning shifts toward competition with tree-structured speculative decoding, adding discussion and citations for Sequoia, EAGLE-2, and OPT-Tree. v2 also adds KV-compression and precision-scaling references. The substantial parameter-sharing discussion and its associated transformer/LoRA references are removed.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the motivation, method, and fidelity prose remain. v2 fixes malformed method wording, condenses and relocates the advantage list, separates ablations into Section 4.4, reorganizes the appendices, and adds an Impact Statement. These are localized editorial and structural revisions rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one column to two. v2 adds the tree/roofline/cost diagram and joint accuracy-throughput plot, redraws the latency display from six panels to two with additional comparators, and revises the draft-length plot. Tables gain baseline rows and new EAGLE/ablation comparisons, while comprehensive throughput results move into Appendix A.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the empirical efficiency case more informative by adding measured EAGLE comparisons, full-precision comparison rows, and an acceptance-rate check across quantizers (Tables 3–8). These address gaps in v1's comparative evidence. The benefit is tempered by removal of concrete large-batch and failed-termination caveats from v1 Appendix C and unresolved inconsistencies in sampling descriptions and numerical summaries.
